statement_source_and_scope_match: SP §1.4 explicitly defines the disorder-averaged second moment and its expected linear growth in 3D. SIM Example 2.1 and Problem 3 supply uniform site disorder and the dynamical question. E §5.3(iii) distinguishes fixed disorder from weak-coupling scaling. The displayed target is two-sided linear comparability, not an asserted exact coefficient or quenched limit. Unit variance fixes the coupling convention; changing the uniform interval rescales lambda.
proposed_statement_text:
Let $(V_x)_{x\in\mathbb Z^3}$ be independent random variables, each uniform on $[-\sqrt3,\sqrt3]$. For $\lambda>0$, define the bounded self-adjoint operator

$$
(H_{\lambda,\omega}\psi)(x)=\sum_{|y-x|_1=1}\psi(y)+\lambda V_x(\omega)\psi(x)
$$

on $\ell^2(\mathbb Z^3)$. Let $\delta_0$ be the unit vector at the origin and set

$$
M_\lambda(t)=\mathbb E_\omega\!\left[\sum_{x\in\mathbb Z^3}|x|_2^2\,
\big|\langle\delta_x,e^{-itH_{\lambda,\omega}}\delta_0\rangle\big|^2\right].
$$

Does there exist $\lambda_0>0$ such that, for every $0<\lambda<\lambda_0$, there are constants $0<c_\lambda\le C_\lambda<\infty$ and $t_\lambda<\infty$ with

$$
c_\lambda t\le M_\lambda(t)\le C_\lambda t\qquad(t\ge t_\lambda)?
$$

The expectation averages the static random potential. The lattice is infinite, the initial state is fixed, and $\lambda$ is held fixed as $t\to\infty$. This asks for the disorder-averaged, order-of-growth form of quantum diffusion for a standard bounded single-site law. It does not prescribe a limiting diffusion coefficient or a Brownian path limit.
applied_significance: This model describes the spreading of an initially localized quantum particle through a crystal with random site energies. Linear growth of the mean-square displacement would justify the diffusive transport scale used to model weakly disordered solids directly from unitary microscopic dynamics. It gives quantitative transport information beyond the existence of extended spectral states.

issues_found: Probability mode is not explicit in Simon’s terse statement.
An exact limiting coefficient would be stronger than the selected order-of-growth target.
Spectral delocalization, time-averaged estimates and weak-coupling limits may be confused with this assertion.
Diffusion-pole papers use the same Anderson terminology and require full scope checks.
Initial duplicate note incorrectly described entry 099 as a random-potential problem.
issues_resolved: Used Spencer’s explicit disorder expectation and unprojected delta initial state.
Kept only positive finite two-sided linear bounds.
Retained fixed positive lambda, infinite lattice and no time averaging; checked ESY and BDH scope.
Read JKS response identities and analyticity caveats and JK coefficient representation/approximation discussion.
Reread entry 099 and corrected its deterministic continuum model.

Unit-variance uniform law is a coupling rescaling of Simon’s box distribution. Spencer’s kinetic normalization differs by a constant energy shift and the parity unitary U psi(x)=(-1)^(x1+x2+x3) psi(x), preserving transition probabilities.
Finite-range hopping makes the second moment finite at each finite time through bounded position commutators.
